overview: The F-16 Hands-On Throttle And Stick (HOTAS) places every function that needs instant access (transmit, designate, weapon release, countermeasures) or must be used while maneuvering on the side-stick controller (SSC) and throttle grip (TQS). Most switches are multi-purpose: what they do depends on the master mode (NAV, A-A, A-G, and the throttle-selected DOGFIGHT / MISSILE OVERRIDE overrides) and on the Sensor Of Interest (SOI). The SOI is the one display/sensor that currently owns the hands-on controls (cursor, TMS, Expand/FOV): on an MFD it is shown by a box drawn around the display edge, on the HUD/HMCS by an asterisk top-left, and any sensor page that is not SOI shows 'NOT SOI'. The DMS moves the SOI (up = HUD, down = MFDs / other MFD); only FCR, TGP, WPN, HAD and HSD formats can be SOI, the HUD only in NAV and A-G, and in A-A the SOI is limited to FCR, HSD and TGP. All A-G sensors share one System Point Of Interest (SPI); after slewing, the standard reset habit is TMS aft (break track), Expand/FOV to wide/normal, then Cursor Zero (CZ OSB). In BMS all HOTAS functions are modelled except the HOBO (hands-on blackout) switch, and short (<0.5 s) versus long presses are modelled as in the real jet.

buttons.name: TRIM Switch (trim hat)
buttons.summary: Hands-on pitch and roll trim of the FLCS.

actions.general: Nose-down pitch trim (changes the hands-off 1 g trim condition).
Nose-up pitch trim. A slight nose-up trim is needed to zero stick force during an 11-13 degree AOA approach.
Left-wing-down roll trim (roll trim also commands rudder through the ARI).
Right-wing-down roll trim.

buttons.bmsNotes: Stick trim is inoperative while the autopilot is engaged (the MANUAL TRIM panel wheels still work) and when AUTO TF is engaged. The Dash-1 notes precise roll trimming is difficult with the stick TRIM button; use the MANUAL TRIM panel wheel for asymmetric stores. BMS also offers a Trim-Reset callback.

buttons.name: Weapon Release Button (WPN REL / pickle)
buttons.summary: Releases or launches the selected weapon; must usually be held through the release sequence.

actions.general: With MASTER ARM in ARM (or SIMULATE), releases/launches the selected store. Hold it down until the release is complete.

byMode.effect: Launches the selected AIM-9/AIM-120; hold the button until the missile leaves the rail (launch nominally 1-2 s). The WPN REL button is always hot for IR missiles. With a bugged target in SLAV, an AIM-120 is fired with a long press.
Press and hold before the solution cue reaches the FPM to give release consent; bombs release automatically when the cue crosses the FPM.
Place the CCIP pipper precisely on the target and press; holding gives a post-designate (delayed) release with a time-to-release delay cue.

First press can designate the target (same as TMS forward); then press and hold for automatic release when the solution cue intersects the FPM. With LASER ARM on and TGP tracking, the press also fires the laser.

Hold for the whole launch sequence: about 1.6 s for a single, 3.2 s or more for a ripple (FPM flashes). JDAM: pickle is hot when in RMAX1-RMIN1, or hold and fly into the DLZ. JSOW/SDB: hot when the weapon reports in-range/in-zone (JIZ).
While the pickle is held the laser fires until the bombs release, then stops even if the button stays pressed.
AGM-65 is always HOT: it launches when pickled regardless of seeker gimbal limits or track validity.

buttons.bmsNotes: The ALT REL button on the front panel works in parallel with WPN REL. A 1.6 s pickle delay is implemented for all IAMs. Emergency/selective jettison also uses a WPN REL press on the S-J page.

buttons.name: Gun / Camera Trigger (2-stage)
buttons.summary: First detent: laser / IR pointer (and recorder in the real jet). Second detent: fires the gun.

actions.general: Fires the TGP laser or IR pointer (or both) for as long as it is held. In the real aircraft the first detent also starts the HUD/video recorder.

byMode.effect: Fire laser (ranging / manual LGB guidance after release) or IR pointer, per the PTR/BOTH setting. Laser requires LASER ARM and valid conditions; IR pointer fires regardless of LASER ARM.
Laser fires only while the trigger is held at the first detent (optional laser ranging for the release solution).

actions.general: Fires the M61 gun (MASTER ARM in ARM) in A-A GUN/EEGS, DGFT and A-G STRAF.

byMode.effect: Fires the gun (EEGS gunsight / funnel); rounds remaining shown on the SMS page.
Laser fires continuously without holding the trigger, until weapon release, submode change, or 30 s.
Laser fire is latched for 30 seconds when the trigger is depressed in CCIP.

buttons.bmsNotes: In BMS the TGP laser/IR pointer is on the first detent; pulling through to the second detent also fires the laser/pointer per the Sniper controls table.

buttons.name: Display Management Switch (DMS)
buttons.summary: Spring-loaded switch that selects the SOI and steps MFD formats.

actions.general: Makes the HUD the SOI (asterisk top-left of HUD) when the HUD is in a mode that allows SOI.

byMode.effect: HUD SOI for HUD markpoints (MARK page).
HUD SOI: slew the TD box / mark cue with the cursor and designate with TMS forward. To reject an AGM-65 VIS target: DMS up then TMS aft.
Not available - the HUD cannot be SOI in the A-A master mode (SOI limited to FCR, HSD, TGP).
Hold: LOOK-INTO-TURN (bank >5 deg shifts the FLIR image into the turn); hold and move the cursor: SNAPLOOK. Image returns to boresight on release (FPM dashed while active).

actions.general: Moves the SOI from the HUD to the MFDs, or from one MFD to the other (if the format there can be SOI).

byMode.effect: Typical way to make the HSD SOI (A-G data link steerpoint, HARM PPT selection, PDLT designation).
In AGM-65 PRE, DMS aft moves the SOI to the WPN page if an FCR FTT is not wanted or fails. In EO-VIS with HMCS, TMS forward or DMS aft moves SOI to the WPN page.
Move SOI to the TGP page before slewing/tracking with the pod.

actions.general: Toggles HMCS symbology blanking on/off. Hands-on blanking overrides HUD and cockpit blanking; while blanked the system behaves as if no helmet is installed (baseline ACM and missile bore).
Steps the primary format of the LEFT MFD through its three format slots (blank formats are skipped).
Steps the primary format of the RIGHT MFD through its three format slots (blank formats are skipped).

buttons.bmsNotes: SOI cannot be assigned in MARK OFLY or in un-stabilized snowplow (SP) pre-designate; in SP the SOI is 'nowhere' until TMS forward. The SWAP OSB swaps MFDs and the SOI box follows the format.

buttons.name: Target Management Switch (TMS)
buttons.summary: Spring-loaded switch for designate (fwd), return-to-search/reject (aft), stepping (right) and IFF/polarity (left) on the SOI.

actions.general: Designate: bug/lock a target, ground-stabilize a cursor or command track on the SOI.

byMode.effect: With the ACQ cursor over a search target: bug it and enter SAM. Designate on the SAM bugged target (or double-designate a search target) = STT. Designate a second target while in SAM = DT SAM. Sequence: RWS > SAM > DT SAM > STT. A quick TMS fwd then aft over the SAM target resumes auto-SAM.

Cursor over a track file or search target: bug it / manually build a track (targets slower than 200 kt are not auto-tracked). Cursor over the bug and designate = STT (other tracks extrapolate for 13 s).

In BORE: hold to inhibit acquisition and slew the boresight cross with the cursor; release to allow lock. With HMCS and FCR SOI, holding slaves the (non-radiating) ACM BORE ellipse to the HMCS aiming cross; the radar radiates and auto-acquires on release. In ACM STT, TMS up does not break lock.

In SP: first press ground-stabilizes the cursor and makes the FCR SOI (pseudo-steerpoint); next press over a return commands FTT (GM/SEA/DBS). In STP sighting: over a discrete return, commands fixed target track (FTT). With AGM-65 PRE and FCR SOI: FTT, then SOI moves to the WPN page (2nd TMS up attempts Maverick track).

A-G: press and release = POINT track on the center of the FOV (falls back to AREA if no edge detail); with AGM-65D/G loaded and POINT track established the pod automatically hands off to the missile. In snowplow: ground-stabilizes the pod. A-A: commands the pod to track the A-A target (TGP LOS becomes independent of the FCR). TGP menu page: select/change the highlighted option.

With the MARK DED page up: records an FCR/TGP markpoint if that sensor is SOI and designating; HUD mark: first press ground-stabilizes the mark cue, second press saves the markpoint. In A-A master mode an OFLY mark is taken immediately (no TMS needed).

Designates the target: ground-stabilizes the TD box (post-designate), after which the TD box can be refined with the cursor. In AGM-65 VIS, SOI then moves automatically to the TGP (priority) or WPN page.

Cursor over a steerpoint/PPT: selects it as steerpoint of interest (A-G data link steerpoint, HARM POS target). Cursor over a Link 16 air track that is not TOI-correlated: designates it as the PDLT (octagon); designate another track to move the PDLT.
PRE: commands AGM-65 track. VIS: stabilizes the TD box / AGM-65 LOS. BORE: stabilizes the AGM-65 LOS. Track and handoff: TMS up and release, confirm correct target.
WPN page SOI in HAS: hands off the threat under the cursor to the selected missile (about 5 s; RDY at OSB 13 when complete - a HARM fired earlier will miss).
Designates the contact under the cursor as primary target; each further designation pushes the previous primary into the priority list (up to 3 priority targets). Handoff is automatic after TMS up.
Steps the weapon flight stage (STRP > LOFT/TRANS/CRUS > TERM); in TERM (generation 2-4) enters ground-stabilized mode / re-locks onto the new aimpoint.
Radar is in ACM: see A-A / FCR ACM (TMS forward = BORE, hold to slave to HMCS).

actions.general: Hold functions: spotlight search, HMCS slaving, HARM submode override, TGP AREA track.

byMode.effect: Hold > 1 s: spotlight search - temporary 4-bar, +/-10 deg scan centered on the ACQ cursor and ANT ELEV setting (slewable). On release the radar reverts to the previous scan, or attempts acquisition if a target is under the cursor. Not available in RWS EXP.
Hold > 1 s: TWS spotlight, centered on the ACQ cursor (overrides TWS bug priority in azimuth/elevation).
Holding TMS forward in any ACM submode commands BORE and inhibits auto-acquisition until release (dead-man). With HMCS: FCR BORE slaved to the HMCS aiming cross while held.
Hold: AREA track (A-G mode only); releasing the switch commands POINT track.

byMode.mode: HUD SOI (A-G DTOS / EO-VIS / IAM-VIS / MARK)
byMode.effect: Hold > 0.5 s: slaves the TD box / mark cue / Maverick LOS to the HMCS aiming cross; move it with head movement, then TMS forward again to ground-stabilize.
TMS up LONG in POS (and on the HAD): cycles the HARM submode (EOM / PB / RUK) - manual override of the automatic selection.
Long press has additional generation-dependent functions - see the Dash-34 man-in-the-loop hands-on controls table.

actions.general: Return-To-Search (RTS) / reject target / break track.

byMode.effect: Steps back one level: STT > DT SAM (if a secondary target is extrapolated) or SAM; DT SAM > SAM; SAM > RWS. Two successive RTS in STT go straight back to RWS.

1st RTS from STT: back to TWS with the target bugged. 2nd: drops the bug. 3rd: dumps all track files (rebuild automatically). 4th: back to RWS. RTS then TMS right-hold (or 3x RTS) clears tracks and returns to CRM search.
The only switch action that breaks an ACM track: drops the track and commands 30x20 NO RAD. Again: 10x60 radiating. Again: 30x20 NO RAD. With HUD SOI and FCR slaved to the HMCS: ACM BORE NO RAD.
Exits FTT/GMTT and resumes the previous search mode (FOV at time of designate); cursor placed at the last tracked position. In SP it only drops the ground target lock.
Breaks POINT/AREA track and returns the pod to SLAVE (slaved back to the radar/SPI LOS); also exits LST. (Dash-34 AGM-65 table lists TGP SOI TMS down as POINT > AREA during Maverick handoff.)
HUD mark in post-designate: cancels ground stabilization and re-ties the mark cue to the FPM. HMCS mark: 1st aft re-slaves the LOS circle to the HMCS aiming cross, 2nd aft re-slaves it to the FPM.

Rejects the designated target and returns to pre-designate (TD box back on the FPM). HMCS DTOS: 1st aft returns the TD box to the HMCS aiming cue, 2nd aft to the FPM (hold > 0.5 s to un-slave from HMCS).
Drops the PDLT. If the HSD cursor is over a preplanned threat with its ring shown, the first press removes that threat ring and a second press drops the PDLT.
Rejects the AGM-65 target (missile returns to its LOS). FCR SOI in FTT: returns to GM/GMT/SEA.
HAS: deselects the handed-off threat; the video reverts to the normal scan cycle.
Over a priority target: removes it from the priority list. Over empty space: resets all priority targets and the designated primary target.
Generation 3-4 in TERM: exits ground-stabilized mode back to non-stabilized.
Radar in ACM: see A-A / FCR ACM (break lock > 30x20 NO RAD / 10x60 cycle).

actions.general: Step: moves the bug / selection to the next item.

byMode.effect: In DT SAM: steps the bug between the primary and secondary target.
Bugs the closest (highest priority) track file; each further press steps the bug to the next priority track. Use it to shoot successive AIM-120s at different tracks.
Changes ACM submode without dropping an existing track (e.g. BORE > 30x20); in ACM STT does not break lock.
With the HUD or A-G FCR as SOI: steps the sighting point rotary (TGT/STP, OA1, OA2, IP, RP) exactly like OSB 10; tracking sensors break lock.
In POINT track: commands AREA track (IR sensor). With an AGM-65D/G handoff: rejects the last handoff target and returns to AREA. TGP menu: moves the selection arrow down.
With a PDLT present: steps the PDLT through DL and radar-correlated tracks (bottom to top, right to left).
AGM-65G with WPN SOI: toggles force correlation (AREA) track.
HAS: selects the first valid threat, further presses step to the next threat/radar. POS: cycles the threats in the selected threat table (hand-off).
Steps through the priority targets (including the designated primary).
Generation 4 in TERM: commands Go Around (SHORT > LONG > OFF). Generation 3-4 in CRUS without autopilot: commands a yaw correction toward the aiming cross.

actions.general: Radar submode transfer between CRM search and TWS.

byMode.effect: From RWS/ULS (with or without SAM, DT SAM or STT) enters TWS and keeps any bugged target.
Returns to the last CRM search submode; the TWS bugged target becomes the SAM target (RWS/ULS) or STT target (VSR). With a bug and system track files it enters DT SAM.

actions.general: Pod / weapon secondary functions.

byMode.effect: Toggles the IR pointer mode: PTR off > PTR highlighted > BOTH > off (CCRP/DTOS until bombs are released).
Generation 2-4 airborne: updates the SPI reference position to the aiming cross.

actions.general: IFF interrogation in A-A; polarity / table toggle on A-G pages.

byMode.effect: AIFF SCAN interrogation of the modes set at OSB 16 (M+ / M1-M4). CPL: beams cover the FCR field of regard; DCPL: all 8 beams, +/-60 deg. Replies shown for 2 s per mode (green circle friendly, yellow square unknown).
FLIR polarity WHOT / BHOT (no effect with TV sensor). TGP menu: moves the selection arrow up.
AGM-65G: polarity COH / BOH (disabled in AREA mode).
Toggles between the three threat tables (same as OSB 2).
Generation-dependent (polarity / antenna / autopilot) - see the Dash-34 man-in-the-loop hands-on table.

actions.general: AIFF LOS interrogation centered on the ACQ cursor (two best beams, range-filtered from the cursor range outward, up to 16 replies shown 1.5 s per mode). Available in any A-A radar mode, even with the FCR in standby.
TGP: changes sensor IR > TV > IR (IR FOV and polarity are remembered).

buttons.bmsNotes: Timing thresholds modelled in BMS: IFF SCAN/LOS split at 0.6 s; spotlight and TWS/CRM transfer at 1 s; HMCS slaving and double-clicks at 0.5 s. When the ICP MARK page is up it takes ownership of TMS forward (markpoint instead of FCR designate).

buttons.name: Countermeasures Management Switch (CMS)
buttons.summary: Hands-on ALE-47 chaff/flare programs and single-point ECM consent.

actions.general: Runs the manual program 1-4 selected on the CMDS PRGM knob. In MAN each press runs it once; in SEMI/AUTO it overrides any automatic program in progress. In BYP any manual request dispenses exactly one chaff and one flare.

Consent. Gives ECM consent to all ECM systems (ECM pod/ATD transmit, ECM ENBL light) regardless of the RF switch, and consent for automatic dispensing: SEMI runs the recommended program once when 'COUNTER' is heard; AUTO dispenses automatically (as sensed) until cancelled with CMS right, expendables are exhausted, or gear is lowered. Consent is remembered even if selected before switching to SEMI/AUTO.

byMode.effect: Enables pod transmissions (verify ECM ENBL light). On the ground the pod only radiates while CMS aft is held.

actions.general: Runs manual program 6 (commonly set up as a flare-only program for close-range A-A or MANPAD defence).

byMode.effect: Cycles the IDIAS operating mode STBY > AVNC (avionics priority) > ECM (ECM priority) > AVNC... AVNC and ECM act as ECM consent.

actions.general: Cancels consent: disables automatic CMDS operation and returns ECM systems (pod, IDIAS) to standby (ECM ENBL light out).

buttons.bmsNotes: Program 5 is on the separate CHAFF/FLARE (slap) button. Moving the RF switch out of NORM cancels a previous consent; returning to NORM does not restore it - CMS aft is required again. ALE-50 towed decoy consent is not modelled.

buttons.name: NWS / A/R DISC / MSL STEP Button
buttons.summary: Nosewheel steering on the ground, air-refuelling disconnect with the AR door open, missile/weapon step in flight.

actions.general: Engages/disengages nosewheel steering (NWS light green on the AR/NWS indicator). Once pressed the button can be released; holding it gives continuous NWS. Do not engage NWS above taxi speed.
A/R DISC: unlatches and releases the tanker boom.
Steps the selected weapon/station or delivery submode.

byMode.effect: Short (< 0.5 s): selects the next station loaded with the current missile type (order 3, 7, 2, 8, 1, 9). Long (>= 0.5 s): selects the next missile category/type in the A-A weapon rotary (e.g. AIM-120 > AIM-9).
Same as A-A: short = next station, long = next missile type.
With a bomb selected: steps the delivery submode CCRP > CCIP > DTOS > CCRP (LADD and MAN are not in the rotary).
Selects the next AGM-65 station; with two stabilized LOS circles, switches between LOS '1' and '2'.
Steps between HARM stations (each station can be preset with its own threat/submode).
Switches stations just like missiles.

buttons.bmsNotes: BMS single callback SimMissileStep covers all three functions (the Cockpit Interaction Guide labels it Missile Step / NWS / A/R Disconnect / A-G toggle). The BMS Training Manual VIP procedure also uses this switch to toggle from the IP to the TGT sighting point.

buttons.name: Paddle Switch (autopilot / fly-up disconnect)
buttons.summary: Temporarily interrupts the autopilot, TFR and fly-ups while held.

actions.general: Interrupts autopilot operation while held (manual control); in ALT HOLD you can depress the paddle, fly to a new altitude and release to set the new altitude reference. Also interrupts TFR / auto fly-ups and roll-to-wings-level fly-ups (disconnects the current TF mode; STBY light on AMS panel).

byMode.effect: Autopilot override / reference change (ALT HOLD, ATT HOLD).
Interrupts a fly-up (an unlatched fly-up resumes on release if the cause persists); also used to hold during the RALT BIT in the TFR check procedure.

actions.general: Autopilot/TF resumes with the new reference; a fly-up that is still commanded resumes.

buttons.bmsNotes: The TRIM/AP DISC switch on the MANUAL TRIM panel is what fully disengages the autopilot. In the two-seat F-16D, use of the paddle switch can cause pitch/roll transients as control is switched between cockpits.

buttons.name: EXPAND / FOV Button (pinky switch)
buttons.summary: Steps through the expanded / alternate fields of view of the SOI.

actions.general: Selects the next available expanded or alternate FOV on the SOI (same as the FOV OSB 3).

byMode.effect: NORM <> EXP: 4:1 expansion in range and azimuth around the ACQ cursor (RWS, SAM, TWS); flashing EXP mnemonic. Auto-exits EXP on STT.
Steps NORM > EXP (4:1) > DBS1 (8:1 resolution) > DBS2 (64:1) in GM; NORM <> EXP in GMT and SEA.
Toggles WIDE <> NARO FOV (FLIR 3.6 deg / 1.0 deg). With the TGP SOI, switching to NARO also puts the AGM-65 WPN page in NFOV.
Steps NORM > EXP1 (2:1) > EXP2 (4:1) around the HSD cursor (HSD must be SOI).
WFOV <> NFOV on the AGM-65 video.
POS: cycles HARM submode (EOM > PB > RUK). HAS: cycles the HAS FOV.
Expanded FOV, as on the HSD.

actions.general: HSD ZOOM (Link 16): independent of SOI, the HSD temporarily changes to the smallest centered range that shows team members 1-4 (symbols 33% larger, ZOOM flashes). Releasing returns to the previous format and range.

buttons.bmsNotes: In BMS the pinky is often used as the DirectX shift key (SimHotasPinkyShift). A quick tap (default < 200 ms, g_nHotasShiftQuickPressTimeLimit) still acts as EXPAND/FOV; holding acts as shift.

buttons.name: Communication Switch (UHF / VHF / IFF OUT / IFF IN)
buttons.summary: Radio transmit (up/down) and IDM / Link 16 data link and declutter functions (left/right).

actions.general: Transmit on the UHF (COM1) radio while held.
Transmit on the VHF (COM2) radio while held.
Hands-on declutter of air-to-air data link symbology.

byMode.effect: IDM: toggles declutter of intraflight data link symbology on the FCR B-scope (stays until pressed again). Link 16: sets the FCR hands-on declutter level (OSB 16 label) to NONE and simultaneously declutters the HUD/HMCS.

actions.general: A-A data link: transmits an IDM A-A request (DMD or ASGN round, mnemonic highlighted 2 s); replies from team members appear on the HSD/FCR. Ignored for 8 s while received messages are displayed.
A-G data link transmit / Link 16 declutter level.

byMode.effect: Link 16 short press (< 0.5 s): cycles the FCR hands-on declutter level ALL > FTR+ > TGTS.
HSD SOI: transmits the selected steerpoint as an A-G data link steerpoint (tone, XMT highlighted at OSB 6); receivers store it in steerpoints 71-80.
FCR SOI in GM/GMT/SEA: transmits the A-G cursor position to the flight (receivers get 'CURSOR'/'DATA' in the HUD and a yellow asterisk).

buttons.bmsNotes: BMS callbacks: SimTransmitCom1 (up), SimTransmitCom2 (down), SimCommsSwitchLeft (IFF OUT, A-A), SimCommsSwitchRight (IFF IN, A-G). IDM uses the UHF/VHF radio, so you cannot talk and data link on the same radio at the same time. The Dash-1 names this the UHF VHF IFF transmit switch.

buttons.name: MAN RNG / UNCAGE Knob (manual range / uncage / gain)
buttons.summary: Rotary for radar gain / TGP zoom / gun range, with a push-button for uncage functions.

actions.general: Mode-dependent analog control.

byMode.effect: Hands-on ground map gain: clockwise increases, counter-clockwise decreases (about +/-20% of the base setting; caret shows gain).
Electronic zoom 1x to 4x (retained between IR/TV sensor changes; shown below OSB 3).
Without a radar lock: sets the manual range of the SNAP bullet circle (700 or 1500 ft).

actions.general: Uncage / mode toggle, depending on the selected weapon or sensor.

byMode.effect: AIM-9: uncages the seeker so it self-tracks (enlarged diamond, track tone); press again to reject the target and re-cage to the BORE/SLAVE LOS.
AIM-9 uncage / re-cage, as in A-A.
Uncages the AGM-65 to blow the dome cover and obtain video (needed for each missile, including AGM-65K/L after alignment; TGM-65G training round too).
A-G mode: toggles Laser Spot Track (LST) mode on/off (same as OSB 20).
Toggles the TI (target isolate) option (same as OSB 10).
NAV/landing modes: press and release for landing declutter (removes roll indicator, ILS bars, flight director, DED data; heading scale moves up). Press again to restore.

buttons.bmsNotes: BMS callbacks SimRangeKnobUp/Down (rotate) and SimToggleMissileCage (press). The knob also accepts analog axis values.

buttons.name: Antenna Elevation (ANT ELEV) Knob
buttons.summary: Manual FCR antenna scan-center elevation / A-G tilt.

actions.general: Clockwise / counter-clockwise from the 0 deg detent moves the antenna scan center up / down to the +/-60 deg limit.

byMode.effect: Sets search scan elevation in RWS/TWS/SAM manual; centers spotlight search and DT SAM scan in elevation. No effect in track modes (STT).
Offsets the antenna tilt angle from the MMC-commanded cursor position.

buttons.bmsNotes: Can be an analog axis (Setup > ANT ELEV) or callbacks SimRadarElevationUp/Down/Center.

buttons.name: RDR CURSOR / ENABLE Control
buttons.summary: Slews the cursor on the SOI; pressing it (Enable / Z-axis) toggles missile BORE/SLAVE and weapon modes.

actions.general: Moves the cursor on the SOI display, referenced to the base of the thumb (tilt left = cursor left).

byMode.effect: Slews the ACQ cursor (captain's bars); over a target shows SAD altitude. Moving it below 5% / above 95% of range bumps the range scale down/up. In SAM moving the cursor disables auto-SAM (manual SAM). Also slews the spotlight scan.
SLEW submode: moves the slewable 60x20 scan center. BORE: with TMS forward held, slews the boresight cross within the HUD FOV. In ACM STT, slewing does not break lock.
Slews the A-G cursor in NORM FOV / the video patch in EXP/DBS; cursor slews move the SPI (zero them with CZ). In SP, slewing is only possible after TMS forward ground-stabilizes the cursor.
In SLAVE: slews the SPI. In POINT/AREA track: slews the pod tracker (POINT track drops while slewing and re-acquires when you stop).
Slews the TD box or mark cue (pre- and post-designate). DTOS post-designate slews are needed for accurate AGR ranging.
Moves the HSD cursor (initialized at the FCR ghost cursor or ownship); bullseye / cursor bearing-range shown; range bumping at the top/bottom edge.
Slews the AGM-65 seeker / cursor to align the video with the target before TMS forward (track).
Moves the captain's bars on the HAS display.
Moves the HAD cursor (as HSD).
With DMS up held: SNAPLOOK view shift. With BSGT selected: slews the HUD FLIR image for boresight.

actions.general: Mode-dependent toggle.

byMode.effect: With AIM-9 or AIM-120 selected: toggles the missile LOS SLAVE <> BORE (changes both missile types). Momentary 'dead-man' (reverts on release) or latched toggle depending on the avionics configuration.
AIM-9 with HMCS: hold to slave the seeker to the HMCS aiming cross (BORE); place it on the target and release/uncage to lock - seeker returns to the FCR/HUD LOS on release in the momentary setting.
WPN SOI: cycles the AGM-65 E-O delivery mode PRE > VIS > BORE.
WPN SOI: toggles between POS and HAS modes.
HMCS coarse alignment: press with the HUD and HMCS crosses aligned to run the alignment (press again to restart if it failed).

buttons.bmsNotes: BMS callbacks SimCursorUp/Down/Left/Right (or Cursor X/Y analog axes) and SimCursorEnable. SimRadarCursorZero is a PC convenience (the real CZ is an MFD OSB). The HMCS momentary vs toggle behaviour for cursor enable is set in the Avionics Configurator.

buttons.name: DOG FIGHT / MISSILE OVERRIDE Switch
buttons.summary: Instant hands-on override of any master mode (except emergency jettison) for close-in or missile fights.

actions.general: Selects the DGFT master mode: gun and missiles together, EEGS gunsight, Attitude Awareness Arc / ghost horizon line, fixed DGFT missile symbology. Configuration (radar mode, weapons) comes from the DTC or the manually programmed DGFT page; default radar is ACM, entered 30x20 NO RAD (not radiating) unless a target was already bugged.

byMode.effect: A quick DGFT-and-back (with ACM programmed) returns the radar to CRM while keeping track on the TWS bugged target.
Cycling DGFT rejects a DTOS/visual designation and resets all AGM-65 targets (any master mode change).

actions.general: Selects the MSL OVRD master mode: missiles only (SMS MSL page identical to AAM), AIM-120/AIM-9 launched against the FCR (or TGP/bore for SRM) line of sight. Not available if no A-A missile is loaded (gun cannot be selected in MSL OVRD).
Cancels the override and returns to the master mode that was selected before (A-A, A-G or NAV). NAV is selected by deselecting A-A/A-G with the switch centered.

buttons.bmsNotes: For HOTAS where the center position has no DX button (e.g. TM Cougar) set g_bHotasDgftSelfCancel 1 so releasing DGFT/MRM automatically calls override cancel; otherwise map SimDeselectOverride to the center. Callbacks SimSelectSRMOverride / SimSelectMRMOverride.

buttons.name: Speed Brake (SPD BRK) Switch
buttons.summary: Thumb slide: aft opens the speed brakes incrementally, forward closes them.

actions.general: Opens the speed brakes incrementally while held; they stop where released. Opening is 60 deg, limited to 43 deg with the right main gear down and locked; hold the switch aft to override the 43 deg limit. After nose gear compression on landing they open fully and stay open.
Speed brakes hold their current position.
Closes the speed brakes in one motion; leave the switch in CLOSE to prevent creeping.

buttons.bmsNotes: In the F-16D the front and rear switches are in parallel: either can override the other by holding OPEN. BMS callbacks AFBrakesOut / AFBrakesIn / AFBrakesToggle.

buttons.name: Throttle Cutoff Release (idle detent)
buttons.summary: Allows the throttle to be rotated outboard and retarded from IDLE to OFF.

actions.general: At IDLE the cutoff release at the base of the throttle must be actuated so the throttle can be rotated outboard and pulled to OFF (engine shutdown). The throttle is also rotated outboard to advance OFF > IDLE (start) and MIL > AB; retarding from AB to MIL rotates it back automatically.

buttons.bmsNotes: BMS callback SimThrottleIdleDetent (toggle IDLE/OFF); on hardware with a physical detent the launcher can set AB and IDLE detent positions. It is the only TQS item with a 3D-cockpit hotspot.

buttons.name: HOBO (Hands-On Black-Out) Switch
buttons.summary: Real-jet cockpit lighting blackout switch - not implemented in BMS.

actions.general: Hands-on blackout of cockpit/exterior lighting in the real aircraft. Not modelled in Falcon BMS (the only HOTAS function that is not).

buttons.name: CHAFF/FLARE Dispense Button ('slap switch', left side panel next to the throttle)
buttons.summary: One-touch manual dispense of CMDS program 5.

actions.general: Manually initiates CMDS program 5 (typically a chaff + flare combination for unexpected threats) in any CMDS mode except OFF/STBY. It is on the left side panel near the throttle, not on the grip.

buttons.bmsNotes: Default key 'S'. Together with CMS forward (programs 1-4) and CMS left (program 6) it gives one-touch control of three programs.
